meta.note: English doesn't start from hello: conversational glue and work vocabulary — what actually powers live speech and AI dialog.

cards.trans: in fact, as it really is
cards.ex_t: Actually, that's not quite what I meant.
To be fair, we had very little time.

cards.note: followed by a bare infinitive: I'd rather stay
cards.ex_t: I'd rather discuss this tomorrow.

cards.note: on, not from — a common Slavic-language calque
cards.ex_t: It depends on the budget.

cards.trans: to the best of my knowledge
cards.ex_t: As far as I know, the deadline hasn't changed.

cards.trans: to work out, to solve by thinking
cards.ex_t: I need to figure out why the numbers don't match.
We came up with a better approach.
She pointed out a flaw in the analysis.
It costs roughly two thousand euros.

cards.note: in analytics: a finding that changes the decision
cards.ex_t: The survey gave us a key insight into user behaviour.

cards.note: does it make sense? = is it clear/logical?
cards.ex_t: Does this chart make sense to you?

cards.note: softer than must: intended, but not guaranteed
cards.ex_t: The report was supposed to be ready yesterday.

cards.note: with a gerund: ended up rewriting everything
cards.ex_t: We ended up rewriting the whole pipeline.

cards.trans: summed up in a few words
cards.ex_t: In a nutshell, sales are up, margins are down.

cards.trans: to reduce the set of options
cards.ex_t: Let's narrow down the options to three.

cards.trans: an exchange of one benefit for another
cards.note: not a compromise: you give up one thing to gain another
cards.ex_t: There's a trade-off between speed and accuracy.
Let me double-check the numbers before we send it.

cards.trans: in the end, after some time
cards.note: false friend: NOT 'possibly' — it means 'sooner or later'
cards.ex_t: Eventually, we found the bug.
We rely on external survey data.

cards.trans: a mild way to accept an argument
cards.ex_t: — We can't afford it. — Fair enough.
